scenarios.description: Resolve a recent Connect recording and use its ID and reader for inspection.
scenarios.userEntryPoint: Run apparent connect list --limit 1 --json or invoke /apparent in an agent with the skill installed.
prerequisites: A candidate CLI, Node 22, a built Connect service and a private working directory.

runner.instructions: From connect/service, build with npm run build, set APPARENT_CONNECT_TEST_BINARY to the absolute candidate CLI path and run node --test test/native/reader-profiles.integration.ts. Run npm test for pending, ordering, access and legacy timestamp coverage.

expectedEvidence: The candidate CLI lists the expected encrypted capture ID, recording timestamp, age and ready status for each explicitly selected reader.
The candidate CLI retrieves and inspects the recording by ID using the approved reader.
limits: The fixture uses a local synthetic Connect service. It does not exercise a live account, agent slash-command registration or Desktop UI.

scenarios.description: Inspect a Connect capture from a shared working directory using a private output path and verify atomic bundle publication.
scenarios.userEntryPoint: Run apparent inspect <capture-id> from a directory that fails a Connect trust check.
prerequisites: A native test build and a private temporary root for the synthetic filesystem fixtures.

runner.instructions: Run cargo test --locked --bin apparent hosted_inspect_. Set APPARENT_TEST_INSPECT_BINARY to an absolute candidate CLI path to exercise a built or packaged executable.

expectedEvidence: An unsafe download destination is named on the first error line, along with the permission failure and a private retry path.
An unsafe reader directory identifies local Connect reader storage and the permission failure.
Both failures omit absolute paths and leave no downloaded capture or staging directory.
From a shared directory, inspect with an explicit private --out and --marks prints the verified bundle's marks. Unsafe, existing and invalid destinations fail before any request.
A local mark inspection during a separate fetch cannot read the unpublished output. It succeeds after the fetch publishes the complete bundle.
limits: The scenarios use synthetic files and a loopback Connect service.

scenarios.description: Differentiate a refused Connect manifest connection from a stalled manifest request.
scenarios.userEntryPoint: Run apparent fetch or apparent inspect against an authorized Connect capture.
prerequisites: A native test build, curl and a private temporary root.

runner.instructions: Build the Connect client TypeScript package and run cargo test --locked --manifest-path connect/client/Cargo.toml hosted_fetch_connection_failures_discover_mcp_without_changing_access.

expectedEvidence: The transport error identifies the manifest phase and distinguishes connection refusal from curl timeout or the client deadline while preserving encrypted relay guidance.
Stalled asset, peer authorization and credential renewal requests identify their phases without exposing the route, endpoint or credential.
A stalled fetch publishes no bundle and exposes no capture ID or local path.
limits: The loopback requests simulate controlled failures. They do not identify the root cause of a production transport incident.

scenarios.description: Measure synthetic Connect share activation through verified readiness and advancing recipient playback.
scenarios.userEntryPoint: Choose Share on a saved recording, then open the ready capability link.
prerequisites: Standard GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04, Node 22.23.0, pinned control and candidate revisions, and a private evidence directory.

runner.instructions: Dispatch the optional hosted benchmark with stream=connect. Follow the owner README for pinned revisions, the synthetic evidence artifact and local diagnostic replay.

expectedEvidence: An unauthenticated recipient verifies the ready manifest, all original assets match the synthetic fixture, and Chromium presents two frames with advancing media time.
A machine-readable receipt distinguishes link availability, watch readiness and advancing playback and records cold/warm milliseconds, trace coverage, resource guards and normalized score.
limits: The loopback lane uses named effect substitutes for the Desktop sender, identity and managed persistence. Chromium is headless and browser HTTP caching is disabled.
CPU accounting and topology describe the hosted Linux guest. Local diagnostic timings are outside the hosted score series.
